fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). Moses led Israel before Joshua (Joshua 1:1–2). So this wasn't Joshua winging it like a man with no recipe. He was following the instructions he'd been given.

The elders are there, standing with all Israel in verse 33, but the text never says they asked for the altar. It says Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). Moses led Israel before Joshua (Joshua 1:1–2). Sometimes the people in the room aren't the people who gave the order.

The Levitical priests do show up in this passage. They carry the ark of the covenant (Joshua 8:33). But the text never says they asked for the altar. It points to Moses, the servant of the LORD, who had commanded it (Joshua 8:31). Good guess, though. Priests and altars go together like dough and a hot oven.

Uncut is right. The Book of the Law of Moses said, "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). Joshua built it according to what was written. I can't leave a cookie alone for five seconds, so I'd have grabbed a tool by now.

Polished sounds fancy, but that's not what the Book said. It called for "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). The word you want is uncut. Joshua built it according to what was written.

Carved isn't what the Book said. It called for "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). So the word you want is uncut. I'd have wanted a little swirl on top, honestly. That's why I'm the stamper and not the one writing the instructions.

True. Joshua 8:31 says, "…on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings." Both kinds are named right there. The text says they built the altar according to what is written in the Book of the Law, and then they offered on it.

Right, the statement is False. Joshua 8:33 says, "All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" Foreigners and citizens alike were in that crowd. Nobody got left in the parking lot.

Bless it is. Half the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, "…as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel." (Joshua 8:33). The text says it was Moses' command, and the blessing is the stated purpose. Two groups, two mountains, all of it for that.

Counting a whole crowd that size would take forever, and I'd lose my place around the fortieth row. The text gives another purpose. They stood there "…as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel." (Joshua 8:33). The word you want is bless.

That's it, baker. Joshua read "…before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them." (Joshua 8:35). The women and the little ones are named right there in the assembly. That's who else was listening.

The passage doesn't name any kings among the listeners. It names who was there: "…the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them." (Joshua 8:35). So the answer is the women and the little ones.
